newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Hog epidemic spreading in Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: Hog epidemic spreading in Taiwan.

text.p: Taiwan's fast-moving foot and mouth epidemic had spread to 716 pig breeding centres as of late Wednesday -- double the number reported on Monday, officials said.
Agriculture officials reported that more than 666,000 diseased and healthy pigs at affected farms would have to be destroyed.
As of Monday, the total was less than 400,000 pigs at 357 farms, according to statistics released by the cabinet's Council of Agriculture.
"We will keep on slaughtering all pigs at infected breeding farms," council secretary-general Lee Jen-chyuan said.
Industry sources quoted by the ruling Nationalist Party estimated that about 15 percent of Taiwan's 11 million swine -- or 1.65 million animals -- would be affected directly.
The farm council banned all pork exports after confirming the outbreak last Thursday, when the virus had been found in just nine of the island's 25,000 hog breeding farms.

The news of Taiwan's sudden halt of pork exports has sent cash pork prices in the United States up more than 5 percent since Thursday and hog futures prices soared as speculators, exporters and retail firms scrambled to secure supplies.

Expectations that Taiwan, one of the top buyers of U.S. corn and soybeans for animal feed, would cut its grain imports by at least 20 percent as it culls its diseased hog herd also prompted selling of grain futures in Chicago.

Across the island, masked soldiers in plastic suits have wielded electric prods to stun pigs and then used huge earth movers to dump them into incinerators or giant pits -- often with the pigs still gasping for air.
